title: Franklin's 200-Year Gift

beats.text: In seventeen ninety, Benjamin Franklin left a strange gift in his will.
One thousand pounds each to Boston and Philadelphia.
The money would be lent to young tradesmen, at interest.
Then the funds would wait. For two hundred years.
He trusted compounding to do the rest.
He never lived to see a penny of it.
But the money kept working, generation after generation.
It helped build a trade school in Boston, and an institute in Philadelphia.
By nineteen ninety, the two funds were worth millions.

caption:
In 1790 Benjamin Franklin left £1,000 each to Boston and Philadelphia, to be lent to young tradesmen, with part of it left to grow for two centuries.

By 1990 the two funds were worth millions.
